rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient that spans nearly the full solvent-strength range at a mid temperature, so we can see the overall elution window and whether any compounds are at risk of being unretained or still retained at 42 min. The 20 min gradient is moderate enough to reveal major resolution problems without being excessively compressed or overly slow.

Only one pair is limiting and the run still finishes before 10 min, so the best next probe is to halve the gradient slope while keeping the same solvent window and temperature. This tests whether the critical pair is slope-responsive; if it opens substantially, we can later trade back some time, and if not, we will know to change temperature or the phi window instead.

The critical pair is strongly slope-responsive: at 40 min all pairs are resolved, so the optimum should lie between 20 and 40 min. A 24 min gradient is the first shorter test that may keep every pair at or above 1.5 while preserving a last peak near or below 10 min.

The critical pair responds to slope, but 24 min was still not enough; a small temperature increase may shift selectivity enough to separate that pair while also pulling the last peak back under 10 min. Using 22 min keeps pressure on run time while probing whether temperature can recover the lost resolution more efficiently than simply lengthening the gradient.

At 45 C the selectivity changed enough to remove the original coelution, but two moderate gaps now limit the score; making the gradient slightly shallower should improve both while likely keeping t_last near 10 min. This is the most direct exploitation step around the current best method.

The 45 C runs suggest temperature is changing selectivity more than slope, but 24 min worsened the late critical pair, so the next efficient move is another small temperature step up while keeping the successful 22 min timing. This should test whether the two subcritical pairs can be pushed above 1.5 without paying a time penalty.

Temperature alone is not solving the selectivity problem, so the next probe should change the phi window while keeping the best tG/T. Trimming to a narrower, more central gradient window should alter selectivity for the clustered middle-late peaks and may improve both subcritical pairs without extending the run.

The best region remains around the full-range window at 45 C, and with 22 min we are very close to the 10 min cutoff; shortening slightly may improve the late pair that worsened on shallower gradients while preserving the beneficial temperature-driven selectivity. This checks whether the optimum is actually a bit steeper than the current best.

The late pair improved when the gradient was made steeper, and the run still has comfortable margin under 10 min, so one more step steeper is a good exploitation test. This will show whether the current best is on the rising side of the optimum or whether 20 min is already near the peak.

At 45 C the only remaining problem is the early-middle pair, and slope changes have not fixed it, which points to selectivity rather than gradient steepness. Testing the same 18 min method at 40 C isolates the temperature effect on that pair while keeping a fast run.

The troublesome cluster is clearly temperature-sensitive, and moving from 45 to 40 C changed which adjacent pair is limiting; one further step cooler may continue that selectivity shift and open the remaining subcritical gap. With t_last still well below 10 min at 40 C, there is room to test 35 C without a time penalty.

A temperature scan around 45 C has been highly nonmonotonic, so it is worth checking whether the critical pair passes through a better selectivity point at lower temperature rather than assuming 35 C is directionally worse. The run remains safely under 10 min, making this a clean selectivity probe at fixed fast slope.

At 30 C the remaining issue is a tight three-peak cluster, and unlike the 45 C case the late peaks are already comfortably resolved, so a slightly shallower gradient should help the under-resolved adjacent pairs without creating a new late problem. The last peak is still under 10 min at 18 min, so there is room for a 20 min test with no time penalty expected.

Changing tG at 30 C worsened the leading pair in the critical cluster, so the next lever should be the gradient window rather than slope. A slightly lower phi1 should keep the cluster within a less aggressive part of the gradient and may improve selectivity there while likely still keeping all peaks under 10 min.

At 30 C the best result came from the steeper of the tested slopes, and lowering phi1 hurt the same critical pair, so the most promising remaining local move is one step steeper at the original full window. The last peak has ample margin under 10 min, so this exploits the current best selectivity while testing whether the leading pair continues to improve.

The 30 C method is the current best and the critical three-peak cluster is clearly temperature-driven, so the next logical test is one more temperature step cooler at the same optimal slope/window. There is still enough time margin to probe whether 25 C gives the selectivity maximum for that cluster while keeping t_last under 10 min.

Since the best point remains 18 min at 30 C and both changing tG and lowering phi1 hurt the same cluster, the remaining useful lever is the starting composition. Raising phi0 one step should shift the crowded early-middle cluster to a different effective phi region and may improve its selectivity while keeping the run within the 10 min target.

Raising phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 improved both runtime and the critical three-peak cluster, so one more step in the same direction is the best remaining local selectivity probe. There is still plenty of time margin, and if the cluster continues to open this could push all adjacent pairs closer to full credit.

The last two runs show a clear trend that increasing phi0 improves the critical cluster and shortens the run, so continuing one more step is the strongest exploitation move. This tests whether we can push both remaining subcritical adjacent pairs closer to or above 1.5 while still keeping all compounds comfortably retained.

phi0 = 0.15 was the best start composition, and pushing it to 0.20 over-compressed the critical pair, so the next local move should keep phi0 at 0.15 and make the gradient one step steeper. The best runs have improved as runtime decreased, so this checks whether we can retain the stronger cluster selectivity at phi0 = 0.15 while gaining still more speed without losing resolution credit.

The optimum appears centered at phi0 = 0.15 and 30 C, but the remaining subcritical pair may prefer a slightly shallower slope than 18 min. Even if this costs some time, t_last at the current best is only 8.0 min, leaving room to test whether improved resolution more than offsets the modest time increase.

The best point is still 0.15/0.95/18/30, and both steeper and shallower slopes worsened the same early cluster, so the remaining practical lever is a modest reduction of phi1 at the best phi0. This narrows the window while keeping the cluster inside the gradient and may shift selectivity enough to raise the weakest adjacent pair.

Reducing phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 shifted which pair is weakest while staying near the best score, so one further step down is the most informative remaining window adjustment around the optimum. This may move the crowded three-peak cluster into a more favorable selectivity region without risking truncation.

With only two injections left, one should probe whether the superior phi0 = 0.15 setting can combine with the alternative 45 C selectivity pattern that previously gave a different limiting pair and strong overall performance. This is the highest-value unexplored crossover near the best region and could reveal a better balance than either temperature family alone.

For the final shot, keep the best phi window and slope and test the last unexplored neighboring temperature on the cool side of the optimum. The temperature response has been nonmonotonic, and 25 C with phi0 = 0.15 could improve the critical cluster beyond the current best while still staying under the 10 min limit.
